title: Pair the lanes
scenario: Pair each swimmer with their lane time, in order.

intro.job: Pair each swimmer with their lane time, in order.

idea.rule: zip walks two lists holding hands — no indexes, no off-by-one.
idea.detail: zip(a, b) hands you the first of a with the first of b, then the second with the second, and so on — as pairs you can unpack straight into two names. There's no index to get wrong. If one list is longer, zip simply stops when the shorter one runs out.

watch.code:
out = []
for n, t in zip(a, [9, 8]):
    out.append((n, t))
print(out)

model_restatement: Match each swimmer with the time at the same position and print the pairs.

clarify.question: Are the two lists always the same length?
Sort by time?
clarify.answer: No — keep them in lane order.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: For each position i, pair the swimmer at i with the next time. Print the pairs.
draft_code:
times = [12, 15]

for i in range(len(names)):

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after iteration 1, what is pairs?

why_line: times[i + 1] is one ahead: ana gets ben's 15, and on ben's turn times[2] doesn't exist.

explain.rule: Indexing one ahead is two kids walking out of step — ana grabs ben's time, and by ben's turn there's no hand left to hold.
explain.bridge: So how could the two lists walk in step, without you counting positions at all?

fix.rule: zip pairs the first with the first, the second with the second — and you never touch an index.

walk.gloss: An empty list for the pairs.
Walk both lists in step: a name and its time together.

fix.recommended:
times = [12, 15]
pairs = []
for name, t in zip(names, times):
    pairs.append((name, t))
print(pairs)

alternatives.code:
times = [12, 15]
pairs = []
for i in range(len(names)):
    pairs.append((names[i], times[i]))
print(pairs)
alternatives.note: Index both with the same i — works, but zip has no index to get wrong.
